LESSON: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do we read narratives? 2. What makes you enjoy reading a narrative?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension,
2. apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information,
3. appreciate reading for purposes of comprehension and information. SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading.
2. Explain Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: read a passage in print or non-print format and answer questions,
4. Show that you can: read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why do we read narratives? 2. What makes you enjoy reading a narrative?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read a passage in print or non-print format and answer questions,
2. Discuss vocabulary from the passage and use them to construct simple sentences,
